cards.text: Here we go, friend! A wise teacher is passing short, sharp sayings to the one he calls 'my son' (Proverbs 23:19), part of the thirty sayings he says he wrote (Proverbs 22:20). He opens with a warning: don't envy wicked men, and don't go wishing for their company.

cards.question: The teacher says not to envy wicked men or want their company. What reason does he give?

answers.text: Their hearts are full of pride

cards.text: Then the teacher switches to building: by wisdom a house is built, and by understanding it's established. I once stacked cookie boxes to the ceiling with no plan at all, and friend, that tower stood for about FOUR seconds.

cards.question: In the teacher's picture, the rooms of that house built by wisdom get filled through knowledge. What are they filled with?

answers.text: Tools for every kind of work

cards.text: Next up, strength. A wise man is strong, and knowledge makes his strength even greater, which is GREAT news for me, because I'm a cookie stamper and knowledge is the ONLY gym I've got.

cards.question: The teacher says to wage war only with sound guidance, because victory lies in a multitude of ___.

cards.text: Then the teacher turns to the fool: wisdom is too high for him.

cards.question: True or false: at the meeting place, the fool opens his mouth and has plenty to say.

cards.text: Then come the plotters: whoever plots evil will be called a schemer. As for a foolish scheme, the teacher doesn't call it a whoopsie, he calls it SIN.

cards.question: The teacher has a word about the mocker too. How do people see a mocker?

cards.text: Then the teacher gives a gut check about the day of distress. You know the day: the bills stack up, the boss calls, and your phone hits one percent.

cards.question: True or false: the teacher says fainting in the day of distress shows how small your strength is.

cards.text: Now comes a hard one. Rescue those being led away to death, the teacher says, and hold back those stumbling toward the slaughter.
Then the teacher pictures someone saying, 'Behold, we did not know about this,' and he answers with questions.

cards.question: Someone says they didn't know about those being led away to death. The teacher answers with a question about who does know. Who is it?

answers.text: The One who guards your life
The king who rules the land
The elders at the city gate

cards.question: The teacher asks one more question about the One who weighs hearts. Will He not repay a man according to his ___?

cards.text: The teacher calls his listener 'my son' and tells him to eat honey, because it's good, and the honeycomb is sweet. Friend, you don't have to tell a cookie stamper twice that sweet things are good.

cards.question: Then the teacher makes his point with the honey. Know therefore that ___ is sweet to your soul.
True or false: the teacher says if you find wisdom, there is a future for you, and your hope will never be cut off.

cards.text: Then the teacher turns and speaks straight to the wicked man. Don't lie in wait near the home of the righteous, he says, and don't destroy his resting place.

cards.question: The teacher says a righteous man may fall seven times. What does the righteous man do?
The righteous man keeps getting back up. But in bad times, the wicked ___.

cards.text: Seven falls and back up every time, friend, and I tip over more than that reaching for the top oven rack, gold base and ALL. Now the teacher says when your enemy falls, don't gloat, and when he stumbles, don't let your heart rejoice.

cards.question: The teacher warns against gloating when your enemy falls. What could happen if the LORD sees it?

answers.text: He would turn His wrath away from your enemy
He would make you fall the very same way
He would raise your enemy up above you

cards.text: So no victory dance, no end-zone spike, put the confetti AWAY. Then the teacher comes back to a warning like his very first one: don't fret over evildoers, and don't envy the wicked.

cards.question: Why not envy them? The evil man has no ___, and the lamp of the wicked will be ___.

cards.text: For his last word, the teacher calls his listener 'my son' again and tells him to fear the LORD and the king.

cards.question: Along with fearing the LORD and the king, who does the teacher say not to associate with?

cards.text: Then the teacher gives his reason to steer clear of the rebellious: it's about what they bring with them.

cards.question: True or false: the teacher says the rebellious will bring destruction slowly.

cards.text: The teacher closes with a question: 'Who knows what ruin they can bring?' Friend, that's advice worth keeping right on the counter.
